messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the 1710636000 deploy we saw a regression in serving latency. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~420ms for the text-generation route and p99 spiked much higher. KV cache hit rate dropped in the same window.
eli: Noted. Any obvious config changes in the rollout? microbatching or kernel flags?
sasha: deploy-bot shows the cohort toggled `kernel_selector=auto_fast` and increased `microbatch_size` from 8 -> 16 for the GPU pool.
maya: @sasha yeah that matches the rollout diff. Also noticed `kv.cache_prefetch` toggled on in the new revision.
jordan: Quick profiling dump attached — I grabbed a single-host perf trace for a warm steady-state:
```
# sample profiler output (summary)
model_forward: 10.4ms
attention_kernels: 95.8ms (was 42.1ms)
kv_lookup: 12.7ms (kv hits: 70% vs 98% baseline)
microbatch_assembly: 3.2ms
rpc_overhead: 1.8ms
```
eli: attention_kernels doubled. That points at kernel selection change -> execution path that's slower for our seq lengths. Also KV hits falling suggests cache eviction behavior changed (maybe microbatching interacts with per-request KV lifecycle).
priya: Log snippet from host (timestamps aligned to deploy):
```
2026-01-15T13:12:04Z INFO serving: starting kernel_selector=auto_fast
2026-01-15T13:12:08Z WARN kv_cache: prefetch enabled, max_entries=50000
2026-01-15T13:12:09Z INFO batching: microbatch_size=16
2026-01-15T13:12:12Z ERROR perf: tail_latency_warning p99=890ms
```
maya: I'm worried auto_fast chose an attention kernel optimized for throughput but with worse latency for our short chat sequences. Increased microbatching probably increased KV churn across workers.
eli: Can we repro locally by toggling kernel_selector to `stable` and microbatch back to 8? If perf returns to baseline then this is configuration-induced.
sasha: I ran a small replay with traffic-generator against the exact commit: kernel_selector=stable + microbatch=8 -> p95 170ms, p99 270ms. With auto_fast + microbatch=16 -> p95 410ms, p99 820ms. Repro is strong.
jordan: Do we have a quick rollback path? The deploy was a config rollout (not model change) so revert should be simple.
oncall: @jordan initiated rollback for deploy 1710636000 at 13:25Z. Rolling config to kernel_selector=stable and microbatch_size=8.
deploy-bot: rollback: deploy 1710636000 -> 1710634800 (config revert) initiated by jordan. status: in_progress
priya: After rollback started, KV cache hit rate climbed back to ~97% within ~40s on the sampled hosts.
eli: Can someone check p95/p99 on the edge for user-facing route?
sasha: Metrics: after rollback p95 ~185ms, p99 ~290ms — basically back to normal. Tail-latency percentiles tracked down to deploy window.
maya: Good. Root cause summary: `kernel_selector=auto_fast` chooses a throughput-oriented attention kernel that regresses single-request tail latency for our common short sequence lengths. Coupled with increasing microbatch_size -> increased cross-request KV churn and cache miss amplification. Auto prefetch made things worse by increasing concurrent memory pressure, evicting KV entries.
jordan: Action items: 1) revert `auto_fast` from config list until we add perf guardrails, 2) add canary p99 gating for kernel selector changes, 3) update rollout playbook to keep microbatch default at 8 for chat routes and require perf benchmark for any change, 4) add a telemetry alert for KV hit-rate drop >5% within a 1m window.
priya: I'll open the follow-up ticket with repro steps and attach the profiler traces.
eli: Suggest also adding a perf check in CI: run short-seq benchmark with both kernel_selector options and compare p95/p99 before rolling wide.
maya: Thanks all — marking incident resolved since rollback restored SLAs. Will follow up with the RFC on kernel selection policies. :white_check_mark:
